GitHub: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1218

When an agent installs a built local package directory into a different project, the directory-copy path can make development dependencies and generated output dominate the work, with no copy-size estimate or hint that an existing packed-artifact path would avoid it.

Observed on published `@unbrained/pm-cli 2026.9.7`, Node 24.19.0, Linux, while validating the public pm-ops package:

- The isolated acceptance test's `pm install <local package checkout> --project --json` exceeded its unchanged 30-second child-process limit twice. Reusing the npm content cache did not resolve it.
- That checkout carried 144 MiB of `node_modules`.
- `npm pack --ignore-scripts --json` produced a 144,565-byte archive with 615,643 unpacked bytes across 25 entries.
- Installing that archive through the existing local-tarball support retained the package-doctor, real CLI routing and host-SDK fallback assertions. The complete installed-CLI test passed in 20.09 seconds. This is the whole test's time, not an isolated installation benchmark, and the timing is host-dependent.

The published `sdk/extension/install-runtime` directory-copy path uses a recursive copy without a filter when the destination is outside the source. This is distinct from the nested-destination bug fixed in #827 and the already implemented tarball support in #844.

Could the local-source install plan expose the copy scope and estimated file/byte count, and suggest `npm pack` plus `pm package install <archive.tgz>` when the directory contains substantial development/generated data? A machine-readable source mode and copy-cost receipt would let agents choose deliberately before starting a bounded operation.

This is an agent-UX request, not a request to silently change local-directory snapshot semantics or weaken install verification. Preserve explicit directory installs, ignored-script policy, runtime dependency resolution and exact host SDK linking. Acceptance should cover both directory and tarball sources and verify that the suggested command works in an isolated project.
GH-1218: expose local package copy scope and packed-install alternatives
Expose a bounded machine-readable local-directory copy-cost plan and a verified packed-install alternative without silently changing directory snapshot semantics.

SDK and CLI local-source planning identifies directory versus archive source and bounded file/byte estimates before copying; large development trees receive a working npm pack and archive-install suggestion; preserve directory snapshots, ignored scripts, dependency resolution, containment and exact host SDK linking; real isolated directory and archive acceptance covers the published consumer flow.
